title.en: Two Mexicans arrested as police uncover big meth lab on South African farm
title.zh: 警方在南非农场发现大型冰毒实验室，两名墨西哥人被捕

summary.en: The overnight raid of the multi-million dollar drug operation took place near the border with Zimbabwe.
summary.zh: 这是一则来自全球栏目的新闻，重点涉及公义、尊严与问责。如需完整细节，请阅读英文原始报道。

body.en:
Two Mexicans have been arrested in South Africa after police uncovered a multi-million dollar crystal methamphetamine laboratory in the north of the country.

The lab was raided overnight at a farm near the town of Musina, in the Limpopo province, near South Africa's border with Zimbabwe. Two Zimbabweans and a Malawian national were also arrested.

Police said it followed a two-month investigation into suspicious activities at the farm. Drugs and equipment worth around 600m rand ($37m; £27m) were seized as well as an undisclosed amount of cash.

A number big meth labs on remote farms have been discovered by South African police over the last two years - with several involving Mexican nationals.

In May, police arrested 11 people, including four Mexicans, after uncovering a suspected drug lab worth $6m on a remote farm north-west of Johannesburg.

In September last year, five Mexicans were arrested after police dismantled a crystal meth lab, with drugs worth $20m, on a farm in the east of the country.

In July 2024, three Mexicans were among those arrested at a remote farm in Limpopo province where a crystal meth lab and drugs worth $108m were uncovered.

The five Musina farm suspects will appear in court on Monday to face charges relating to the manufacture and possession of illicit drugs.

"The discovery has exposed an alleged sophisticated, industrial-scale operation believed to have been established for the manufacture of dangerous illicit substances destined for distribution," the police said in a statement.

South Africa is as one of the largest crystal meth consumer markets in the world, according to the 2022 Global State of Harm Reduction report.

The UN says its geography and "porous borders" also make it an ideal transit point for illicit drug.

South Africa is not the only African country where illicit laboratories have been found.

In May this year, Nigeria's drug enforcement agency said it had "dealt another crippling blow" and dismantled "a highly sophisticated, multi-million-dollar Nigerian-Mexican methamphetamine production syndicate".

The lab at the centre of an ongoing court case was discovered in a dense forested area of the West African nation.

Counter-narcotics officials at the US-Africa Command (Africom) recently told the BBC that since 2023 14 Mexican-operated laboratories had been raided on the continent - found in Kenya, Mozambique, Nigeria and South Africa.

Experts believe this indicates criminal cartels in Mexico are increasing using Africa, not just as a trafficking hub, but also as a production base.
body.zh: 警方在南非北部发现了一个价值数百万美元的冰毒实验室后，两名墨西哥人在南非被捕。 该实验室位于林波波省穆西纳镇附近的一个农场，该农场位于南非与津巴布韦边境附近，连夜遭到突击搜查。两名津巴布韦人和一名马拉维国民也被捕。 警方表示，这是在对农场的可疑活动进行了两个月的调查之后进行的。价值约 6 亿兰特（3700 万美元；2700 万英镑）的毒品和设备以及数额不详的现金被查获。 过去两年，南非警方在偏远农场发现了多个大型冰毒实验室，其中几个涉及墨西哥公民。 5 月，警方在约翰内斯堡西北部的一个偏远农场发现了一个价值 600 万美元的可疑毒品实验室，逮捕了 11 人，其中包括 4 名墨西哥人。 去年9月，警方在该国东部一座农场拆除了一个冰毒实验室，其中藏有价值2000万美元的毒品，五名墨西哥人被捕。 2024 年 7 月，三名墨西哥人在林波波省的一个偏远农场被捕，那里发现了冰毒实验室和价值 1.08 亿美元的毒品。 穆西纳农场的五名嫌疑人将于周一出庭，面临与制造和持有非法药物有关的指控。 警方在一份声明中表示：“这一发现揭露了一个据称复杂的工业规模运作，据信该运作是为了制造用于分销的危险非法物质。” 根据 2022 年全球减少危害状况报告，南非是世界上最大的冰毒消费市场之一。 联合国表示，其地理位置和“漏洞百出的边界”也使其成为非法毒品的理想中转站。 南非并不是唯一发现非法实验室的非洲国家。 今年5月，尼日利亚缉毒机构表示，它“再次遭受严重打击”，并捣毁了“一个高度复杂、价值数百万美元的尼日利亚-墨西哥甲基苯丙胺生产集团”。 正在审理的法庭案件的中心实验室是在这个西非国家的茂密森林地区发现的。 美国-非洲司令部 (Africom) 的缉毒官员最近告诉 BBC，自 2023 年以来，非洲大陆已有 14 个墨西哥经营的实验室遭到突击搜查，分别位于肯尼亚、莫桑比克、尼日利亚和南非。 专家认为，这表明墨西哥的犯罪卡特尔正在越来越多地利用非洲，不仅将其作为贩运中心，而且将其作为生产基地。

title.en: Rosenberg: Shortage of petrol but not patriotism as Russians feel growing impact of war

summary.en: Drivers are waiting hours in fuel queues, as Moscow prepares to celebrate Russian Flag Day.
summary.zh: 这是一则来自全球栏目的新闻，重点涉及和平与克制。如需完整细节，请阅读英文原始报道。

body.en:
At a petrol station in the south-east of Moscow, Svyatoslav has been queuing in his car for two hours.

"They say there will be petrol here," Svyatoslav tells me optimistically. "They just don't know when. Maybe today, maybe tomorrow."

Even if he had, there'd be no quick fuel fix for Svyatoslav. This week across Moscow, and in other parts of Russia, there have been long queues for petrol.

Those repairs have been triggered by Ukrainian drone strikes on Russian oil facilities. Such long-range attacks sparked major fuel shortages earlier this summer. The targeting of oil refineries has continued apace.

This time the queues in Moscow are even longer than before. The authorities appear to be struggling to resolve problems with refining capacity and logistics.

"The second wave of the fuel crisis is building," declared broadsheet Nezavisimaya Gazeta this week.

Driving around Moscow this week two things catch the eye: patriotic announcements on giant billboards about Russian Flag Day…and giant petrol queues.

"Last night I went to get petrol at 11pm," says Elizaveta who's queuing again for fuel. "By midnight I'd reached the front of the queue. Then they shut the petrol station until 2am."

"I drove into Moscow yesterday from the provinces," says Lyubov. "It was empty petrol stations all the way."

"Everyone says there is a difficult situation in the country," Lyubov tells me. "Everyone connects this to that situation."

Before Russia's full-scale invasion of Ukraine in 2022 there were no drone attacks on Russian oil refineries - or on any facilities inside Russia. These strikes haven't forced the Kremlin to U-turn. It's continuing what it still calls the "special military operation", Russia's war on Ukraine.

That is extraordinary for a country widely recognised as an energy superpower and one of the world's leading exporters of crude oil.

To reduce the fuel shortage the government has also temporarily authorised the production and sale of lower-grade petrol, like Euro 2, which is faster to produce. Euro 2 contains up to 50 times more sulphur than modern Euro 5 and was banned in Russia in 2013.

"For modern cars," wrote the government newspaper Rossiyskaya Gazeta, "regular use of lower-grade petrol can increase the pressure on the fuel injector, spark plugs, oxygen sensors, the catalytic converter and soot filter. Euro 2 won't kill an engine on one re-fuelling. But it sharply reduces the margin of safety."

It's not just the targeting of oil facilities which have brought the war home to Russians.

title.en: 'We are devastated' - Nigerian villagers bury bodies after overloaded boat capsizes
title.zh: '我们心都碎了'——尼日利亚村民在超载船只倾覆后埋葬遇难者遗体

summary.en: Officials report that an overloaded boat carrying villagers, including many children, to rice farms capsized, leading to multiple fatalities and widespread devastation among the community.
summary.zh: 官员报告称，一艘载有村民（包括许多儿童）前往稻田的超载船只倾覆，导致多人死亡，社区遭受广泛破坏。

body.en:
At least 48 people have died in Nigeria after an overloaded boat with an estimated 70 passengers capsized on a river in a remote area of north-western Sokoto state.

"We are devastated at the moment," Hussaini Shehu, a resident of Gorau village, told the BBC, explaining that the accident had happened on Thursday morning as people were heading out to their rice farms along the banks of the river.

Photos taken at the village mosque show many of the recovered bodies wrapped in mats and traditional cloths ahead of their burial. It is believed that so far around 10 people have been rescued.

Bashir Usman Gorau, a lawmaker the area, told the BBC that many of the victims were children.

In farming communities, children often accompany their parents to farms to help with agricultural activities - and at the moment the community is harvesting rice.

The authorities say search and rescue efforts are continuing as people are still missing - and teams worked through the night.

The remote location, poor access and unreliable mobile phone coverage has made it difficult to get information.

Gorau said the wooden vessel had been overloaded but had also developed a leak "through which water gushed in".

But Shehu said the security services had not been able to get to them as an armed group had been active nearby on Thursday.

Heavily armed criminal gangs - which loot and kidnap for ransom - operate across parts of north-west and north-central Nigeria. The insecurity makes accessing remote areas difficult and has forced lots of communities to abandon their homes.

A militant jihadist group called Lakurawa has also been active in Sokoto and neighbouring Kebbi state.

Last December, US President Donald Trump and the Nigerian government launched airstrikes in Sokoto, saying they were targeting Islamic State militants. IS has not linked itself to Lakurawa as it has done with other groups in the region that it backs.

Boat accidents are common in Nigeria, with overcrowding, poorly maintained boats and weak enforcement of safety rules often blamed for deaths. At least five people drowned when a boat overturned in Jigawa state last month .

In January, at least 26 people drowned when a boat carrying farmers and fishermen from Jigawa to Yobe state capsized.

And in December 2024, 54 bodies were recovered from the River Niger after a boat that may have been carrying more than 200 passengers capsized.

The authorities have recommended measures including providing safer boats and life jackets, dredging waterways, deploying water guards at jetties and terminals, and ensuring boat operators are properly trained and licensed.

But many of these measures have not been fully implemented or properly enforced.

body.zh: 尼日利亚索科托州西北部偏远地区一艘载有约 70 名乘客的超载船只在河上倾覆，造成至少 48 人死亡。 戈劳村的居民侯赛尼·谢胡 (Hussaini Shehu) 告诉英国广播公司：“我们此刻感到非常震惊。”他解释说，事故发生在周四早上，当时人们正前往河边的稻田。 在村庄清真寺拍摄的照片显示，许多找到的尸体在下葬前都用垫子和传统布料包裹着。据信目前已有约10人获救。 该地区议员巴希尔·乌斯曼·戈劳 (Bashir Usman Gorau) 告诉英国广播公司，许多受害者是儿童。 在农业社区，孩子们经常陪父母去农场帮忙做农业活动——目前社区正在收割水稻。 当局表示，由于仍有人员失踪，搜救工作仍在继续，救援人员彻夜工作。 由于位置偏远、交通不便以及手机信号覆盖不可靠，获取信息变得困难。 戈劳说，这艘木船已经超载，但也出现了泄漏，“水从其中涌入”。 但谢胡表示，安全部门未能找到他们，因为周四附近有一个武装团体在活动。 全副武装的犯罪团伙在尼日利亚西北部和中北部部分地区进行抢劫和绑架以索取赎金。不安全局势使得进入偏远地区变得困难，并迫使许多社区放弃家园。 一个名为 Lakurawa 的激进圣战组织也在索科托和邻近的凯比州活跃。 去年12月，美国总统唐纳德·特朗普和尼日利亚政府对索科托发动空袭，称他们的目标是伊斯兰国武装分子。 IS 并未像其支持的地区其他组织那样与 Lakurawa 建立联系。 船只事故在尼日利亚很常见，过度拥挤、船只维护不善以及安全规则执行不力常常被认为是导致死亡的原因。上个月，吉加瓦州一艘船翻覆，造成至少五人溺水身亡。 1月份，一艘载着农民和渔民从吉加瓦开往约贝州的船只倾覆，造成至少26人溺水身亡。 2024 年 12 月，一艘可能载有 200 多名乘客的船只倾覆，在尼日尔河中打捞出 54 具尸体。 当局建议采取的措施包括提供更安全的船只和救生衣、疏浚水道、在码头和码头部署水卫，以及确保船只操作员接受适当的培训和许可。 但其中许多措施尚未得到充分实施或适当执行。 对于数百万尼日利亚人来说，特别是在农村社区，河流...

reflection.en: The profound grief felt by the Nigerian villagers burying their loved ones, especially the children, reminds us of the deep sorrow that accompanies such sudden loss. In moments of devastation, the promise that Yahweh will one day wipe away every tear and that death, mourning, crying, and pain will be no more offers a future hope beyond present suffering.
reflection.zh: 尼日利亚村民在埋葬他们所爱之人，特别是儿童时所感受到的深切悲痛，提醒我们这种突如其来的损失所带来的巨大哀伤。在遭受毁灭性打击的时刻，雅伟有一天将擦去所有眼泪，死亡、悲伤、哭泣和痛苦将不复存在的应许，为我们提供了超越当前苦难的未来盼望。

verse.textEn: He will wipe every tear from their eyes. There will be no more death or mourning or crying or pain.
verse.textZh: 神要擦去他们一切的眼泪；不再有死亡，也不再有悲哀、哭号、疼痛。

title.en: North Korea: Will Trump-Kim talks happen anytime soon?
title.zh: 朝鲜：特金会很快就会举行会谈吗？

summary.en: As Donald Trump claims a meeting is planned with Kim Jong Un, North Korea's response sends a signal that it wants maximum concessions in return for talks with the US.
summary.zh: 这是一则来自全球栏目的新闻，重点涉及真理、分辨与诚实。如需完整细节，请阅读英文原始报道。

body.en:
As Donald Trump claims a meeting is planned with Kim Jong Un, North Korea's response sends a signal that it wants maximum concessions in return for talks with the US.

North Korea responded on Thursday to claims by US President Donald Trump that he will be holding talks with leader  Kim Jong Un later in the year with a broadside of ballistic missiles .

The South Korean military said Pyongyang launched 10 short-range missiles that landed in the sea off North Korea's east coast. 

This came a day after Kim's powerful sister, Kim Yo Jong, said Pyongyang was "completely unaware of" plans for discussions.

Trump's announcement on Wednesday that he is in contact with Kim and that the two leaders would meet later in the year appears to have caught Pyongyang off guard. It comes after the US president said the military would scale back annual military drills with South Korea.

The statement by Kim Yo Jong, director of the Central Committee of the Workers' Party of Korea and one of her brother's closest advisers, dismissed Trump's decision to dramatically scale back the 10-day Ulchi Freedom Shield exercises as "unworthy of comment and [we] have no interest in it at all."

"After Trump's overtures, Kim Yo Jong effectively said downscaling exercises is not enough, and North Korea launched about a dozen missiles in its third firing in two weeks," Leif-Eric Easley, a professor of international studies at Ewha Womans University in Seoul, told DW.

In a statement carried by the state-run Korea Central News Agency (KCNA), Kim Yo Jong mocked South Korea as a "puppet" and indicated that only canceling the drills in their entirety would be seen as a "goodwill measure."

Choo Jae-woo, a professor of foreign policy at South Korea's Kyung Hee University, told DW that unlike in Trump's first term, Pyongyang right now is in a position of power and will likely seek more guarantees before coming to the negotiating table.

"North Korea is not interested in dialogue because Kim was humiliated in 2019 when Trump walked out of their talks in Hanoi," said Choo said.

Those talks ended in acrimony over the US insistence that North would have to scrap its nuclear program.

Pyongyang has since forged a close security and economic alliance with Russia , granting it access to military technology, energy and consumer goods previously beyond its grasp under international sanctions.

"They are in the safe hands of Russia and China and, in the years since Hanoi, Kim has made it his regime's official position that North Korea will never engage in dialogue as long as giving up its nuclear weapons is part of the discussion,” Choo added.

body.zh: 正如唐纳德·特朗普声称计划与金正恩会面一样，朝鲜的回应发出了一个信号，即它希望获得最大限度的让步，以换取与美国的谈判。 朝鲜周四回应了美国总统唐纳德·特朗普的说法，即他将在今年晚些时候与领导人金正恩举行大规模弹道导弹会谈。 韩国军方表示，平壤发射了 10 枚短程导弹，落在朝鲜东海岸附近的海域。 此前一天，金正恩有权势的妹妹金与正表示，平壤“完全不知道”讨论计划。 特朗普周三宣布他正在与金正恩接触，两位领导人将在今年晚些时候会面，这似乎让平壤措手不及。此前，美国总统表示，军方将缩减与韩国的年度军事演习。 朝鲜劳动党中央委员会主任、她哥哥最亲密的顾问之一金与正在声明中驳斥了特朗普大幅缩减为期 10 天的乙支自由之盾演习的决定，称其“不值得评论，[我们]对此完全没有兴趣”。 首尔梨花女子大学国际研究教授莱夫·埃里克·伊斯利 (Leif-Eric Easley) 告诉德国之声：“在特朗普做出示好之后，金与正实际上表示缩减演习规模还不够，朝鲜在两周内的第三次发射中发射了大约十几枚导弹。” 在国营朝鲜中央通讯社 (KCNA) 发表的一份声明中，金与正嘲笑韩国是“傀儡”，并表示只有完全取消演习才会被视为“善意措施”。 韩国庆熙大学外交政策教授秋在宇 (Choo Jae-woo) 告诉德国之声，与特朗普第一个任期不同，平壤目前处于强势地位，可能会在坐上谈判桌之前寻求更多保证。 “朝鲜对对话不感兴趣，因为 2019 年特朗普退出河内会谈时，金正恩受到了羞辱，”Choo 说。 由于美国坚持要求朝鲜必须放弃其核计划，这些谈判以激烈的方式结束。 此后，平壤与俄罗斯建立了密切的安全和经济联盟，使其能够获得此前因国际制裁而无法掌握的军事技术、能源和消费品。 “它们在俄罗斯和中国的安全手中，自河内以来的这些年里，金正恩已将其政权的官方立场表明，只要放弃核武器是讨论的一部分，朝鲜就永远不会进行对话，”秋补充道。 伊斯利表示，平壤不太可能同意与美国进行谈判，至少在短期内……

title.en: Pakistan ex-PM Imran Khan back in jail after hospital examination
title.zh: 巴基斯坦前总理伊姆兰·汗在医院检查后重返监狱

summary.en: It comes as the court had earlier this week ordered that he had to be taken for a hospital examination.
summary.zh: 这是一则来自全球栏目的新闻，重点涉及公义、尊严与问责。如需完整细节，请阅读英文原始报道。

body.en:
Pakistan's former Prime Minister Imran Khan was moved back to prison early on Friday after being examined by doctors at a hospital in Islamabad, who deemed him "medically fit".

Khan was seen by "a team of qualified doctors" including an ophthalmologist, a cardiologist and a physician, Pakistan's Information Minister Attaullah Tarar said.

The Supreme Court had on Tuesday ordered the cricketer-turned-politician be taken to a specific private hospital within 48 hours to be examined by physicians, following complaints about his health.

The intervention was the most significant relief Khan has received from the courts since he was imprisoned in 2023 on corruption charges, which he says were politically motivated.

As well as being transferred to hospital, the court order also specified Khan should be allowed to see his family, which he has not been able to do in months. On Tuesday night, his sister Noreen Khan visited him in prison.

His other sister Dr. Uzma Khan accompanied him during the hospital visit last night. She was present throughout all stages of the medical examination overnight on Thursday, Tarar said.

Khan was meant to be sent to the private Shifa Interational Hospital in Islamabad, according to the Supreme Court order.

The area around it was sealed off with barriers, with officers and police vans in place. Outside, the BBC saw cars being moved with a truck to clear the street while police cars and armoured vehicles patrolled.

Some PTI activists had gathered along the route and near the hospital, despite warnings from the court and party leaders not to.

But Tarar later confirmed Khan had not been taken there and was instead driven to the government-run Pakistan Institute of Medical Sciences (PIMS) hospital. A senior police official told the BBC the security presence outside Shifa was a decoy.

Tarar said the change had been made due to the "security situation created by PTI workers".

The PTI's Information Secretary Sheikh Waqas Akram asked: "Was the court order implemented in its true spirit, or was it merely a superficial exercise for propaganda?"

Khan's lawyers have said he is suffering from various health conditions, including poor eyesight, and has been unable to access specialist medical care.

In February, the 73-year-old's lawyer said his client had 15% vision left in his right eye after prison authorities failed to take action - an allegation the government disputed.

In Tuesday's court order, the panel wrote: "We are mindful of the constitutional and legal obligation... to safeguard the life, health, dignity and security of the prisoner."

Khan, who previously captained the Pakistan national cricket team, served as the country's prime minister from 2018 to 2022.

body.zh: 巴基斯坦前总理伊姆兰·汗在伊斯兰堡一家医院接受医生检查后，于周五早些时候被送回监狱，医生认为他“身体状况良好”。 巴基斯坦信息部长阿塔拉·塔拉尔表示，汗接受了“一组合格的医生”的诊治，其中包括一名眼科医生、一名心脏病专家和一名内科医生。 在接到有关这位板球运动员出身的政治家的健康投诉后，最高法院周二下令在 48 小时内将这位板球运动员送往一家特定的私立医院接受医生检查。 此次干预是汗自 2023 年因腐败指控入狱以来从法院获得的最重大救济，他表示腐败指控是出于政治动机。 除了被转移到医院外，法院命令还规定汗应该被允许见他的家人，但他已经几个月无法见到家人了。周二晚上，他的妹妹诺琳·汗 (Noreen Khan) 去监狱探望了他。 他的另一个妹妹乌兹玛·汗医生昨晚陪同他去医院探望。塔拉尔说，周四晚上，她参加了体检的所有阶段。 根据最高法院的命令，汗本应被送往伊斯兰堡的私立希法国际医院。 周围地区已被路障封锁，并有警察和警车就位。在外面，英国广播公司看到一辆卡车正在移动汽车以清理街道，而警车和装甲车则在巡逻。 尽管法院和政党领导人警告不要这样做，但一些 PTI 活动人士还是沿着路线和医院附近聚集。 但塔拉尔后来证实汗没有被带到那里，而是被送往政府运营的巴基斯坦医学科学研究所（PIMS）医院。一名高级警官告诉英国广播公司，希法外的安全人员是一个诱饵。 塔拉尔表示，做出这一改变是由于“PTI 工作人员造成的安全局势”。 PTI 信息秘书谢赫·瓦卡斯·阿克拉姆 (Sheikh Waqas Akram) 问道：“法院命令是按照其真实精神执行的，还是只是表面上的宣传活动？” 汗的律师表示，他患有多种健康问题，包括视力不佳，并且无法获得专业医疗护理。 今年 2 月，这位 73 岁老人的律师表示，由于监狱当局未能采取行动，他的当事人的右眼视力只剩下 15%，但政府对这一指控提出了异议。 在周二的法院命令中，专家组写道：“我们铭记宪法和法律义务……保护囚犯的生命、健康、尊严和安全。” 汗曾担任巴基斯坦国家板球队队长，并于 2018 年至 2022 年担任该国总理。 他于 2023 年 8 月入狱，并面临以下指控……

title.en: Bodies of two hikers missing for decades found after Swiss glacier melts
title.zh: 瑞士冰川融化后，两名失踪数十年的徒步旅行者遗体被发现

summary.en: Officials have announced the discovery of the bodies of two Belgian hikers who went missing in 1992. Their remains were found after the Trift Glacier in Switzerland receded significantly.
summary.zh: 官员宣布，两名于1992年失踪的比利时徒步旅行者的遗体已被发现。他们的遗骸是在瑞士特里夫特冰川大幅消退后被找到的。

body.en:
The bodies of two Belgian men who went missing in the Swiss Alps in 1992 have been discovered after being exposed by the melting of a glacier, police have said.

A hiker discovered the bodies on 26 July on the Trift Glacier, south of the Swiss city of Lucerne, officials said.

DNA analysis later confirmed them to be those of two mountaineers who went missing 34 years ago near the Weissmies mountain, police said. They were aged 39 and 41 at the time of their disappearance.

Many scientists attribute a rapid retreat in Switzerland's glaciers - which shrunk by a quarter in the decade to 2025, according to Glacier Monitoring in Switzerland (Glamos) - to climate change.

Police in Switzerland's Valais region said in a statement that they had organised a recovery operation following the discovery of the two men's bodies and transferred them to a hospital in the canton's capital, Sion, for identification.

Peaking at over 4,000 metres, the Weissmies mountain - which the two men went missing in the vicinity of - is a popular mountaineering spot in the Saas Valley.

Regional officials maintain a database of missing people dating back to 1925. The majority of people on it disappeared in the moutains, or in rivers and other bodies of water, police said.

The force noted that this was not the first time that the melting of glaciers had exposed the remains of people who had gone missing several decades prior.

In 2023, human remains found on a glacier close to Switzerland's famed Matterhorn were confirmed to be those of a German climber who had been missing since 1986.

The rate of glacier shrinkage has been increasing globally since the 1990s and at a particularly accelerated rate since 2000, according to the European Commission's monitoring body Copernicus.

This melting has been particularly pronounced in Switzerland. Data from Glamos , external reported a further glacier reduction of 3% across 2025, following record years of ice loss in 2022 and 2023.

The upward trend in global average temperatures has brought unseasonably warm weather to Switzerland's higher altitudes, and a reduction in snow has imperilled some of its ski resorts and competitions.
body.zh: 警方称，1992 年在瑞士阿尔卑斯山失踪的两名比利时男子的尸体因冰川融化暴露在外，现已被发现。 官员称，7 月 26 日，一名徒步旅行者在瑞士卢塞恩市南部的特里夫特冰川上发现了这些尸体。 警方称，DNA 分析后来证实，这些人就是 34 年前在韦斯密斯山附近失踪的两名登山者。他们失踪时分别为 39 岁和 41 岁。 许多科学家将瑞士冰川的快速退缩——根据瑞士冰川监测机构 (Glamos) 的数据显示，到 2025 年为止的十年里，冰川缩小了四分之一——归因于气候变化。 瑞士瓦莱州警方在一份声明中表示，在发现这两具尸体后，他们组织了一次打捞行动，并将他们转移到该州首府锡永的一家医院进行身份识别。 韦斯密斯山 (Weissmies mountain) 的山峰海拔超过 4,000 米，两人失踪的地点就在附近，这里是萨斯谷 (Saas Valley) 的热门登山地点。 地区官员维护着一个可追溯到 1925 年的失踪人员数据库。警方称，该数据库中的大多数人都在山区、河流和其他水体中失踪。 该部队指出，这并不是冰川融化第一次暴露出几十年前失踪人员的遗骸。 2023 年，在瑞士著名的马特洪峰附近的冰川上发现的人类遗骸被确认为一名自 1986 年以来失踪的德国登山者的遗骸。 根据欧盟委员会监测机构哥白尼的数据，自 20 世纪 90 年代以来，全球冰川萎缩的速度一直在加快，自 2000 年以来，冰川萎缩的速度尤其加快。 这种融化在瑞士尤为明显。 Glamos 的数据显示，继 2022 年和 2023 年创纪录的冰损失之后，到 2025 年，冰川将进一步减少 3%。 全球平均气温的上升趋势给瑞士高海拔地区带来了反常的温暖天气，降雪量的减少也危及了瑞士的一些滑雪胜地和比赛。

reflection.en: The discovery of these hikers after decades reminds us that there is a time for everything under heaven, even for long-hidden truths to come to light. For families who have waited so long, this revelation, though sorrowful, can bring a measure of closure and peace after years of uncertainty.
reflection.zh: 这两位徒步旅行者在失踪数十年后被发现，提醒我们天下万事皆有定时，即使是长期隐藏的真相，也有显露的一天。对于那些等待了如此之久的家庭来说，这一发现虽然令人悲伤，却能在多年的不确定之后带来一定程度的了结与平安。

verse.textEn: There is a time for everything, and a season for every activity under the heavens.
verse.textZh: 凡事都有定期，天下万务都有定时。

title.en: Why is Israel's military presence growing in Syria?
title.zh: 以色列在叙利亚的军事存在为何日益增长？

summary.en: The article reports on Israel's increasing military presence in Syria, detailing multiple incursions, including a recent attack on an airbase. Local residents in southern Syria describe being detained, having infrastructure destroyed, and the establishment of Israeli military bases.
summary.zh: 这篇文章报道了以色列在叙利亚日益增长的军事存在，详细描述了多次入侵，包括最近对一个空军基地的袭击。叙利亚南部的当地居民称，他们被以色列军队拘留，基础设施被摧毁，并且以色列还在当地建立了军事基地。

body.en:
The recent Israeli attack on a Syrian airbase is just one of many Israeli incursions into Syria. In southern Syria, locals say Israeli troops have detained them, destroyed infrastructure and set up military bases.

It's been two years, four months, 24 days and five hours, said Syrian man Ahmad Hassan al-Din when asked how long it's been since he last saw his son.

In April 2024, Israeli soldiers took Saddam, who had just turned 17, from farmland near the Golan Heights, a part of Syria Israel has occupied since 1967.

"Saddam had gone to feed the animals early in the morning," al-Din, who's from the village of Jubata al-Khashab in the Quneitra district near Golan, told DW. "I called him on the phone, and he told me, 'Everything's fine.' But then later we saw with our own eyes how they took the boy, handcuffed and shackled."

Al-Din filmed Israeli soldiers marching his son through fields. The video, which he forwarded to DW, has previously been verified by open-source investigators at France24 and by human rights organizations.

"They said they took him because he was trespassing on the territory of the state of Israel," al-Din continued. "Even though that area is our farmland and we have a valid UN permit to work there."

To enter this buffer area, Syrian farmers and shepherds needed a special pass from the United Nations Disengagement Observer Force, or UNDOF. The latter was set up to make sure Israeli and Syrian forces kept their distance after a 1974 disengagement agreement.

Humanitarian organizations have since discovered Saddam, now 19, is likely in a prison in Israel.

DW asked the Israeli military what Saddam had been charged with and under which legal system. A spokesperson sent DW a statement similar to one previously sent to other media outlets and human rights organizations that said Israel detains Syrians that it suspects might wish it harm. The statement did not specify whether the army considered the farmer's son to be one of those individuals.

Since Saddam was taken, the Syrian teenager's story has become one of many similar accounts in this part of southern Syria .

After the fall of the country's dictatorial Assad regime in December 2024, Israel took control of the UN-patrolled demilitarized zone. Senior Israeli politicians declared the 1974 agreement void and said troops would be in the area temporarily to protect Israel from cross-border attacks.

However, since then Israel's presence in Syria has become more permanent. In November 2025, UNDOF told reporters Israel had set up 10 bases in the area. From these bases, Israeli soldiers are making near-daily incursions into the Syrian provinces of Daraa and Quneitra.

body.zh: 以色列最近对叙利亚空军基地的袭击只是以色列对叙利亚的众多入侵之一。在叙利亚南部，当地人称以色列军队拘留了他们，摧毁了基础设施并建立了军事基地。 当叙利亚男子艾哈迈德·哈桑·丁被问及距离上次见到儿子有多久了时，他说，已经两年零四个月二十四天零五个小时了。 2024 年 4 月，以色列士兵从戈兰高地附近的农田带走了刚满 17 岁的萨达姆，戈兰高地是以色列自 1967 年以来占领的叙利亚的一部分。 来自戈兰高地附近库奈特拉区朱巴塔哈沙布村的阿尔丁告诉德国之声：“萨达姆一早就去喂动物了。” “我给他打电话，他告诉我，‘一切都很好。’但后来我们亲眼目睹了他们如何带走这个男孩，并给他戴上手铐和脚镣。” 阿尔丁拍摄了以色列士兵带着他的儿子穿过田野的镜头。他转发给德国之声的这段视频此前已得到 France24 开源调查人员和人权组织的核实。 “他们说他们逮捕他是因为他侵入以色列国领土，”丁继续说道。 “尽管那个地区是我们的农田，而且我们拥有有效的联合国许可证，可以在那里工作。” 要进入这个缓冲区，叙利亚农民和牧羊人需要获得联合国脱离接触观察员部队（UNDOF）的特别通行证。后者的设立是为了确保以色列和叙利亚军队在 1974 年达成脱离接触协议后保持距离。 此后，人道主义组织发现现年 19 岁的萨达姆很可能被关在以色列的一所监狱中。 德国之声询问以色列军方，萨达姆被指控什么罪名以及依据何种法律制度，一名发言人表示他们将进行调查。截至撰写本文时，尚未有进一步回应。 自从萨达姆被抓获后，这名叙利亚少年的故事就成为叙利亚南部这一地区许多类似的故事之一。 2024年12月该国独裁的阿萨德政权垮台后，以色列控制了联合国巡逻的非军事区。以色列高级政界人士宣布 1974 年协议无效，并表示军队将暂时驻扎在该地区，以保护以色列免受跨境袭击。 然而，从那时起，以色列在叙利亚的存在变得更加永久。 2025年11月，观察员部队告诉记者，以色列已在该地区建立了10个基地。以色列士兵几乎每天都从这些基地入侵叙利亚的德拉省和库奈特拉省。 “这些入侵通常涉及在人口稠密地区进行装甲巡逻，然后在主要道路上设立临时检查站，所有经过的叙利亚平民都会被拦截、搜查、询问，并扣留他们的手机……

reflection.en: The ongoing military actions and their impact on local communities in Syria highlight the enduring hardship faced by those caught in prolonged conflict. Even amidst devastation and sustained loss, the Scriptures remind us that Yahweh's mercies are new every morning, offering a steadfast hope. This truth encourages us to seek daily strength and compassion...
reflection.zh: 叙利亚持续的军事行动及其对当地社区的影响，凸显了那些卷入长期冲突的人们所面临的持久困境。即使在毁灭和持续的损失中，圣经提醒我们，雅伟的慈爱每早晨都是新的，带来坚定的盼望。这一真理鼓励我们为所有受此类危机影响的人寻求每日的力量和怜悯。

verse.textEn: Because of Yahweh's great love we are not consumed, for his compassions never fail. They are new every morning.
verse.textZh: 我们不至消灭，是出于雅伟诸般的慈爱；是因他的怜悯不至断绝。每早晨这都是新的。

title.en: Alaska charter flight crash kills 8
title.zh: 阿拉斯加包机坠毁致8人死亡

summary.en: A small Cessna 441 plane operated by a private charter company crashed near a US military-managed radar site in Alaska, reportedly killing all eight people on board.
summary.zh: 一架由私人包机公司运营的小型塞斯纳441飞机在阿拉斯加一处由美军管理的雷达站附近坠毁，据报道机上所有八人全部遇难。

body.en:
A small ‌Cessna 441 plane operated by a private charter company crashed near a US military-managed radar site in Alaska. All on board have reportedly died.

A charter plane crash at a remote military radar site in western Alaska on Thursday has left all eight people on board dead, according to the United States   military.

The aircraft  crashed around 12:15 pm (2015 UTC) on approach to Cape Newenham Long Range Radar Site Airport, located about 725 kilometers (450 miles) west of Anchorage, Alaska's largest city, from where it had departed.

Six passengers and two pilots were aboard the plane during the incident, said Clint Johnson, Alaska region chief of the National Transportation Safety Board (NTSB).

Reports identified the plane as a ‌Cessna 441 operated by Anchorage-based air charter company Security Aviation.

Alaska Senator Lisa Murkowski expressed her condolences, following news of the crash.

"I've traveled extensively with Security Aviation throughout Alaska, and have met many of their experienced pilots," she said on X, naming the charter company that operates in the remote region.

She added that multiple agencies, including the US Coast Guard, NTSB, Alaska State Troopers, and the Rescue Coordination Center had responded to the crash.

The Associated Press cited the US ​military's Alaskan Command as saying that the plane was a "civilian-contracted aircraft."

The passengers on board were "dedicated professionals carrying out a vital mission in a demanding environment," AP quoted Lt. Gen. Robert Davis, commander of Alaskan Command, the Alaskan North American Aerospace Defense Command Region and Eleventh Air Force, as saying in a statement.

The specifics of what work the crash victims were doing at the radar site —  which tracks aircraft operating in Alaskan airspace — was not immediately clear from the Alaskan Command's statement.

"This is a devastating loss for our military family and the communities we serve," Davis said, according to AP.

body.zh: 一架由私人包机公司运营的小型塞斯纳 441 飞机在阿拉斯加美军管理的雷达站附近坠毁。据报道，船上所有人均已死亡。 据美国军方称，周四，一架包机在阿拉斯加西部的一个偏远军事雷达站坠毁，机上八人全部遇难。 这架飞机于中午 12 点 15 分（世界标准时间 2015 年）左右坠毁，当时正飞往纽文纳角远程雷达站机场，该机场位于阿拉斯加最大城市安克雷奇以西约 725 公里（450 英里）处，起飞地。 美国国家运输安全委员会（NTSB）阿拉斯加地区负责人克林特·约翰逊（Clint Johnson）表示，事故发生时飞机上有六名乘客和两名飞行员。 报道称，这架飞机是一架塞斯纳 441 飞机，由总部位于安克雷奇的包机公司 Security Aviation 运营。 阿拉斯加州参议员丽莎·穆尔科斯基在得知坠机事件后表示哀悼。 她在 X 节目中说道：“我随安全航空公司走遍了整个阿拉斯加，并遇到了许多经验丰富的飞行员。”她提到了在偏远地区运营的包机公司。 她补充说，包括美国海岸警卫队、国家运输安全委员会、阿拉斯加州警和救援协调中心在内的多个机构已对坠机事件做出了反应。 美联社援引美军阿拉斯加司令部的话说，这架飞机是一架“民用合同飞机”。 美联社援引阿拉斯加司令部、阿拉斯加北美防空司令部和第十一空军司令罗伯特·戴维斯中将的话说，机上的乘客是“在严苛环境中执行重要任务的敬业专业人员”。 阿拉斯加司令部的声明中并未立即明确坠机受害者在雷达站点（该雷达站点跟踪在阿拉斯加领空运行的飞机）所做的具体工作。 据美联社报道，戴维斯说：“这对我们的军人家庭和我们服务的社区来说是毁灭性的损失。” 不要让算法隐藏新闻。如果您信赖我们团队的可信报道，请花点时间点击此处并点击“星标”或“首选”按钮，选择我们作为您在 Google 上的首选来源，这样您始终会首先看到我们经过验证的新闻。

reflection.en: The sudden loss of eight lives in this tragic plane crash brings profound sorrow to many. In moments of such unexpected grief, we are reminded of the promise that Yahweh will one day wipe away every tear, and death, mourning, crying, and pain will be no more. This hope anchors us, even as we grieve the present reality of loss.
reflection.zh: 这场悲剧性的飞机坠毁事件，八条生命的突然逝去，给许多人带来了深切的悲痛。在这样突如其来的悲伤时刻，我们被雅伟有一天将擦去我们一切眼泪的应许所提醒，那时死亡、悲哀、哭号和疼痛都将不再有。这份盼望成为我们的锚，即使我们正为眼前的逝去而悲伤。

verse.textEn: He will wipe every tear from their eyes. There will be no more death or mourning or crying or pain.
verse.textZh: 神要擦去他们一切的眼泪；不再有死亡，也不再有悲哀、哭号、疼痛。

title.en: What Europe's shrinking rivers reveal, and why Australia should take notice
title.zh: 欧洲河流萎缩揭示了什么，以及澳大利亚为何应引起关注

summary.en: Discoveries from Europe's shrinking rivers highlight environmental challenges that extend globally, prompting other regions like Australia to observe and learn.
summary.zh: 欧洲河流萎缩所揭示的发现，指出了远远超出该大陆的挑战。

body.en:
In northern Bulgaria, water in the Danube River has fallen so low that scientists say an ancient mammal has once again been exposed to the world.

The remains of what is believed to be a woolly mammoth were uncovered in late July and hailed by historians as a "very important" discovery.

Near the Serbian village of Prahovo, the rusted vessels and broken masts of German warships also resurfaced from the riverbank this month.

"This has literally never happened before; these wrecks ... have never been visible like this. They've always been completely submerged; what we're seeing now is utterly unprecedented," he said.

The discoveries along Europe's second-longest river come as parts of central and eastern Europe experience prolonged summer heatwaves and drought conditions.

Armin Fojskic, a member of the Zenica Fishermen Association, said if conditions don't ease, he expects a large number of fish to die in European rivers.

"Low levels of water are critical for the fish, especially if it is extremely low, and these past days it has really been extremely low," Fojskic said.

"The main danger for fish is oxygenation of the river; when water flow drops, the river loses oxygen and fish start to suffocate."

According to the European Drought Observatory, about half of Europe and the United Kingdom experienced drought at various levels of intensity in July. Major wildfires have also burned across the continent .

But Peter Gleick, a hydro-climatologist and co-founder of the Pacific Institute in California, believes what Europe has experienced is not in line with normal weather fluctuations.

"Weather is always variable. We always have droughts. We always have floods somewhere at some time ... but what we're seeing now is extreme events worsened by human-caused climate change," Gleick told SBS News.

"We're dumping greenhouse gases into the atmosphere. We know that's warming the planet. We know that it's altering these extreme events by making them more extreme, more frequent, and more intense."

Gleick said the extreme patterns affecting rivers in Europe are similarly impacting water systems across the globe.

"In the western United States, the Colorado River, which is ... shared by seven [US] states and Mexico, is at record low levels," he said.

"Some of the largest reservoirs in the world are built on the Colorado River, and they're now at record lows."

Nick Bond, the director of freshwater ecosystems at La Trobe University, said the Murray-Darling Basin, Australia's largest river system, has been in decline for decades .

title.en: Morocco: Migrants caught between Ceuta dreams and reality
title.zh: 摩洛哥：移民在休达梦想与现实之间挣扎

summary.en: In Fnideq, Morocco, a city bordering Spanish-controlled Ceuta, many aspiring migrants hold onto dreams of crossing over for a better life. However, local residents who have witnessed recent large-scale migration surges caution against the extreme dangers involved in such attempts.
summary.zh: 摩洛哥城市弗尼迪克毗邻西班牙控制的休达。在弗尼迪克，许多渴望移民的人梦想着越境寻求更好的生活，但目睹了近期大规模移民潮的当地居民警告说，这样做风险极高。

body.en:
The Moroccan city of Fnideq is next to Spanish-controlled Ceuta. In Fnideq, would-be migrants dream of crossing to a better life, even as locals who witnessed recent mass migration surges say it's way too risky.

There are only a few kilometers between the city of Fnideq in Morocco and the Spanish enclave of Ceuta — but the distance between those who dream of crossing that divide and those who chose to stay in Morocco is far greater than that.

After July 30, when an estimated 72,000 people crossed from Morocco into Ceuta, there were further calls on social media for people to come to Fnideq for another mass crossing  attempt in mid-August.

That is despite the fact that around  100 people died in the July attempt and that most of those who crossed into Ceuta have since returned to Morocco. Numbers are unclear but somewhere between 2,000 and 8,000 of those who managed to get over to the Spanish enclave remain there. According to reports, they are now living in desperate circumstances . Many are sleeping on the beach while they wait for Spanish authorities to decide their fate.

Still, back in Morocco, some would-be migrants continue to hope for a chance to get to Ceuta.

Malika came to Fnideq from the city of Casablanca in western Morocco with her two children after she heard that people had managed to get there on July 30; she did not want to give DW her full name for personal reasons.

Malika heard there might be a new opportunity to cross in August so she has stayed in Fnideq, together with her 3-year-old daughter and 8-year-old son. For the past few weeks, she says she has simply wandered the streets searching for ways to feed her children. The family has slept in the open.

But rumors about an August crossing also reached both Spanish and Moroccan authorities. On August 15, eyewitnesses reported a heavy Moroccan security presence around Ceuta and Melilla, another Spanish exclave to the east, with numerous checkpoints, patrol boats monitoring the coast and water cannons stationed at the border. Moroccan police said they arrested 111 people as they tried to enter Ceuta. 

"I'm in a situation where I might do something to myself at any moment," she told DW. "My children are starving. I'm practically homeless. I have no job and no stable home, and my husband suffers from depression due to extreme poverty. Sometimes he just disappears, leaving me alone with the two children, without money or shelter."

That is why she still wants to get to Ceuta, she says, where she is certain she and the children will find support of some kind: "Our situation is very difficult. … that's why I want them to go to Ceuta. They will study there and we will be fine."

reflection.en: The longing for a better life, as seen in the dreams of migrants near Ceuta, is a profound human desire. Yahweh's ancient command to love and welcome the foreigner reminds us to see the dignity and hope in those seeking new beginnings, even amidst the inherent risks. This calls for compassion and understanding for all who are displaced.
reflection.zh: 摩洛哥边境移民对美好生活的向往，反映了人类内心深处的渴望。雅伟古老的诫命，要爱护和欢迎寄居者，提醒我们即使在固有风险中，也要看到那些寻求新开始的人的尊严和希望。这呼唤我们对所有流离失所者抱有同情和理解。

title.en: Trump and Kim's renewed bromance stirs new and old threats for Australia
title.zh: 特朗普和金正恩的“兄弟情”重燃，给澳大利亚带来新旧威胁

summary.en: Former US President Donald Trump's independent foreign policy actions, including reducing military drills and engaging with North Korea, have led Asia-Pacific allies to express doubts about the reliability of US defense agreements.
summary.zh: 美国前总统唐纳德·特朗普的独立外交政策行动，包括削减军事演习和与朝鲜接触，导致亚太盟友对美国防务承诺的可靠性产生疑问。

body.en:
Donald Trump's recent appeals to the reclusive North Korean dictator Kim Jong-un have cast doubt on the United States' commitment to its allies in Asia and the Pacific — potentially adding to regional instability, experts worry.

Trump has also reignited fears about North Korea's nuclear test program and whether the US would ever back down on opposing the nation's weapons, which would have broad ramifications.

A decision by the US on Monday to "substantially reduce" the scope of ongoing joint military exercises with South Korea and Japan may have sent a ripple of doubt about the strength of the many interlinked defence ties in the region, and caught some off guard.

Trump announced the decision on social media , saying the exercises were costly and "send a signal that is totally inappropriate and hostile" to North Korea. The totalitarian state had previously complained about the joint military drills, saying they would respond with a new level of deterrence.

But the decision, which came somewhat out of the blue, was made at the same time as Trump is signalling plans to meet with the North Korean leader, raising questions about where their unusual relationship actually sits.

South Korean president Lee Jae Myung said on Wednesday he recognised Trump's "will and efforts to create conditions for dialogue" with North Korea through the reduction of the exercise.

"President Trump's message this time feels like a major decision made with careful consideration to create peace on the Korean Peninsula, moving beyond hostility and confrontation," he wrote on social media.

Joshua Kurlantzick, senior fellow for Southeast Asia and South Asia at the US think tank the Council on Foreign Relations, told SBS News the US decision was in one way unsurprising, given its stated foreign policy shift away from global hegemony and toward influence over the "Western hemisphere" alone.

However, he said it was another significant step toward the potential "fading" of the US defence umbrella as allies "no longer feel" that umbrella is as "reliable as it used to be".

"As a result, and this includes Australia, they are taking various measures." He said this includes strengthening regional defence ties and increasing military spending.

That said, United States Studies Centre CEO and former National Security Council director for Asia, Michael Green, told SBS News that "the hub-and-spoke" US regional strategic alliance network "survives" the Trump administration as there's "no other option".

title.en: 'They'll pay the price': Aussie travel hotspot's new tourist tax
title.zh: “他们会付出代价”：澳大利亚旅游热点的新旅游税

summary.en: Even travellers who have already paid in full could be caught out, according to an industry group.

body.en:
The Fijian government will introduce a new tourism services tax for large-scale tourism operators next month, with travel industry experts warning that the costs could be passed on to customers.

The 5 per cent tax will apply from 1 September. The change has been criticised by travel associations in Fiji, Australia and New Zealand, who claim they were not properly consulted.

The Australian Travel Industry Association (ATIA) said the measure could catch out travellers who have already booked trips to Fiji from September onward, as travel agents and operators face confusion over how to administer the tax.

"The design and roll out reflect a complete lack of understanding of how the travel booking ecosystem works, and it is travellers and travel businesses who will pay the price for that failure," ATIA CEO Dean Long said.

"Travellers are the ones left exposed. Families with September school holiday bookings already paid in full, and travellers on large group, corporate and film production bookings, are being asked to find extra money for a holiday they thought was settled months ago. That is not how you treat people who chose Fiji in good faith."

The change forms part of wider taxation amendments enacted as part of Fiji's 2026-2027 national budget, passed last month.

It will affect tourism operators — including hotel, tourism and cruise businesses — with an annual turnover above FJ$2 million (approximately $1.3 million).

According to Fijian finance minister Esrom Immanuel, revenue from the tax will be used to support Fiji Airways.

"The revenue generated will be ring-fenced and fully directed to Fiji Airways, which continues to face financial pressure from rising aviation fuel costs and its ongoing recovery from losses incurred during the COVID-19 pandemic," Immanuel told local media in June.

It's reported that the tourism tax will generate around FJ$70 million ($44.7 million) for the airline. The Fijian government is the largest shareholder of Fiji Airways.

ATIA confirmed it will meet with the Fijian government to discuss the tourism services tax, which it said arrived with "zero consultation".

Long said there is ongoing confusion over how the tax is collected, saying that members of the travel industry in Australia and New Zealand — which represent Fiji's largest tourism markets — were not consulted on the change.

"None of this needed to happen. The tax arrived with zero consultation with the travel industry in Australia or New Zealand despite the significant importance of these markets to Fiji," he said.

summary.en: Three activists in Hong Kong have been found guilty of inciting others to subvert state power under a national security law introduced by China.

body.en:
Two Hong Kong activists who organised annual vigils to commemorate the 1989 Tiananmen Square crackdown have been found guilty of inciting others to subvert state power under the city's controversial national security law.

Lee Cheuk-yan, 69, and Chow Hang-tung, 41, face a maximum penalty of 10 years in prison after being convicted under the China-introduced law. Sentencing is expected at a later date.

Lee and Chow "incited other persons to organise, plan, commit or participate in acts by unlawful means with a view to subverting the state power", according to a summary on Friday. Chow told the court in May the law itself was on trial.

Hong Kong used to be one of the only places in Chinese territory where people could gather to mark the deadly 1989 crackdown against pro-democracy protesters.

Authorities banned these gatherings in 2020, citing Covid-19 policies, but they have never resumed. This was also the year the national security law, which makes illegal a wider range of dissenting acts, officially came into force.

In mainland China, authorities have banned even oblique references to the 1989 crackdown.

In the courtroom, Chow smiled as the verdict was read out, while Lee showed little emotion as he made a heart gesture and folded his hands to show his gratitude to those in the gallery.

Lee, a lawmaker, and Chow, a lawyer, were also leaders of the now-defunct Hong Kong Alliance (HKA), which has been described as a "toxic tumour" by Chinese authorities.

The HKA was founded in May 1989 to support students holding pro-democracy rallies. Weeks later, the Communist Party crushed pro-democracy protests in Beijing's Tiananmen Square with troops and tanks. Estimates of the death toll range from a few hundred to many thousands.

Over the next three decades, HKA called on authorities to accept responsibility for the crackdown, free dissidents and introduce democratic reform.

Rights group Amnesty International has said the case "relies on vague, overly broad and arbitrary definitions of 'subversion'".

Sarah Brooks, Amnesty International's deputy regional director, said Chow and Lee had "not committed any recognisable crime".

"Chow Hang-tung and Lee Cheuk-yan are prisoners of conscience who should never have been prosecuted in the first place. They must be released immediately and unconditionally," she added.

Elaine Pearson, Asia director at Human Rights Watch, said the convictions showed "how public displays of mourning have become a crime in Hong Kong".

In a separate case, Chow was arrested in June 2021 for "inciting" the public to take part in that year's vigil and later found guilty.

However, Hong Kong's top court overturned that conviction in 2022 , with a judge ruling the police hadn't properly justified the vigil's ban.

summary.zh: 这是一则来自中国栏目的新闻，重点涉及公义、尊严与问责。如需完整细节，请阅读英文原始报道。

body.en:
The two pro-democracy Tiananmen activists were found guilty of inciting subversion. The high-profile case has been widely criticized for highlighting the deterioration of freedom of expression.

A Hong Kong court on Thursday convicted two pro-democracy Tiananmen activists under Beijing's  controversial national security law for "incitement to subversion."

Lee Cheuk-yan, 69, and Chow Hang-tung, 41, had organized candlelight vigils to mark Beijing's deadly 1989 Tiananmen crackdown. They were charged in 2021 and both pleaded not guilty.

They face a maximum prison term of 10 years and are expected to be sentenced at a later date.

Germany and France on Friday morning  published a joint statement to say that both "deeply regret the guilty verdict against human ​rights lawyer and democracy activist Chow Hang-tung."

The statement called for the immediate release of Chow and added that "peaceful advocacy for human rights does not constitute a crime."

Taiwan's Mainland Affairs Council, which oversees the island's China policy, expressed "deep regret and sorrow" and called on the Chinese Communist Party and Hong Kong government to "immediately release those detained in this case." 

Hong Kong judicial officials claimed the pair "incited other persons to organize, plan, commit or participate in acts by unlawful means with a view to subverting the state power."

Prosecutors had argued they "endanger(ed) national security in the name of human rights."

Public commemorations of the deadly Tiananmen crackdown , when Beijing sent troops and tanks to crush protests calling for political reform in and around the capital's Tiananmen Square, have been effectively banned since the 2020 imposition of the national security law on Hong Kong.

The controversial law came after Hong Kong's massive anti-government, pro-democracy protests in 2019.

title.en: After two decades, China is preparing its boldest Moon mission yet
title.zh: 中国正准备执行二十年来最雄心勃勃的探月任务

summary.en: China is preparing its most ambitious moon mission in two decades, scheduled for next month. The mission aims to explore the lunar surface, specifically searching for water.
summary.zh: 中国正准备在下个月执行其二十年来最雄心勃勃的探月任务。此次任务旨在探索月球表面，特别是寻找水资源。

body.en:
How do you explore a place where the sun never shines? China's space program will soon embark on one of the most innovative lunar exploration missions in recent years.

We’ve known for nearly two decades that some form of water exists on the moon. What we still don’t know is exactly how much accessible water ice lies inside permanently shadowed craters, how deeply it is buried or what form it takes.

What we do know is that accessing that water ice will be a real challenge: it is found at the bottom of deep, hard-to-traverse craters where the sun never shines, remaining untouched for billions of years at temperatures well below –200C. These are among the most valuable places on the moon, but the hardest to reach and explore.

Lunar exploration has come a long way since the Soviet Union’s Luna-1 probe reached the moon's vicinity in January 1959. The Apollo missions and their successors showed the challenge is no longer simply to reach the moon. It is to explore places human and conventional rovers cannot easily go, and ultimately determine whether the moon itself can provide some of the resources that future explorers will need.

China has spent two decades building an increasingly ambitious lunar exploration program, named after Chang'e, the ancient Chinese goddess of the moon. The Chang'e-7 mission is expected to set course for our celestial neighbour later this month, although a recent failure involving a different Chinese rocket has introduced some uncertainty over the launch date. Here’s what makes this latest mission so interesting.

The mission will test several novel approaches to lunar exploration. It will consist of an orbiter, a lander, a rover and a hopper.

In addition, the Queqiao-2 lunar relay satellite is already in place. Launched separately in March 2024, it subsequently supported the Chang'e-6 mission and will facilitate communication between Earth and the lunar surface during the Chang'e-7 mission.

We don’t know precisely where the mission will land, but a site on or near an illuminated ridge close to the Shackleton crater in the Lunar South Pole’s Aitken region is a prime candidate.

The hopper will be the mission’s real star. Unlike a wheeled rover, it’s designed to leap over broken terrain and descend into craters where sunlight never reaches, places conventional vehicles may simply be unable to enter.

Adding it to the mission makes sense, given the steep crater walls, broken terrain, permanent shadow and the need for autonomous navigation and communications.

title.en: Indonesia-China naval drill raises neutrality concerns
title.zh: 印尼与中国海军演习引发中立担忧

summary.en: Indonesia's participation in a limited naval exercise with China near Taiwan has raised questions about its long-standing nonaligned foreign policy.
summary.zh: 印度尼西亚与中国海军在台湾附近举行了有限的海上演习，这引发了对其长期不结盟外交政策的担忧。

body.en:
Indonesia maintains a nonaligned foreign policy, but Jakarta's limited participation in a low-level naval exercise with China's navy near Taiwan has drawn scrutiny.

On August 12, an Indonesian frigate briefly joined a naval exercise with China's People's Liberation Army Navy (PLAN) in waters off Taiwan's east coast, with Taipei asking Jakarta for a reason why it joined the drill.

Indonesian Navy frigate KRI I Gusti Ngurah Rai joined the PLAN guided-missile frigate Honghe for what Jakarta described as a "passing exercise." The maneuvers took place during Taiwan's annual Han Kuang military drill. 

An Indonesian Ministry of Foreign Affairs spokesperson said they were fully aware that the exercise's location "made it particularly sensitive," but stressed that its vessel's presence "was simply part of its transit route back to Indonesia." According to the Taipei Times , the Indonesian vessel was returning from Vladivostok, Russia after an exercise with the Russian navy.  

Taiwan's Mainland Affairs Council condemned Beijing's "provocation" after China announced the drill on August 11. Taipei also requested "further details from the Indonesian government" from its Ministry of Foreign Affairs.  

Beijing considers Taiwan to be Chinese territory and has vowed to "reunite" the self-ruled island with the mainland, by using force if necessary . The People's Liberation Army has ratcheted up pressure on Taiwan with frequent military exercises around the island, especially since former US House Speaker Nancy Pelosi visited Taipei in 2022.

Amid reactions from Taipei and Washington, the Indonesian Navy stated that its activities with the Chinese Navy were "not warfighting activities in nature" and "not intended as combat training."

Ying-Yu Lin, an associate professor at Taiwan's Tamkang University Graduate Institute of International Affairs and Strategic Studies, told DW that the Chinese exercise with Indonesia had little tactical significance.

"It wasn't as practical as a joint maritime drill, but China wanted to claim its capability in the waters," he said.

However, Ratih Kabinawa, a visiting research fellow at the Japan Institute of International Affairs focusing on Taiwan-Indonesia ties, told DW that regardless of the significance of the drills, Indonesia should have expected some reaction from Taiwan .

"Like it or not, Indonesia is now dragged into this kind of geopolitical gambit," she said.

body.zh: 印度尼西亚维持不结盟的外交政策，但雅加达有限地参与与中国海军在台湾附近举行的低级别海军演习，引起了密切关注。 8月12日，一艘印度尼西亚护卫舰短暂参加了与中国人民解放军海军在台湾东海岸附近海域举行的海军演习，台北向雅加达询问其参加演习的原因。 印度尼西亚海军护卫舰 KRI I Gusti Ngurah Rai 与中国海军导弹护卫舰红河号一起进行了雅加达所说的“穿越演习”。这次演习是在台湾一年一度的汉光军演期间进行的。 印度尼西亚外交部发言人表示，他们完全意识到演习地点“使其特别敏感”，但强调其船只的存在“只是其返回印度尼西亚的过境路线的一部分”。据《台北时报》报道，这艘印尼舰艇在与俄罗斯海军演习后正从俄罗斯符拉迪沃斯托克返回。 中国8月11日宣布演习后，台湾陆委会谴责北京的“挑衅”。台北还要求外交部“提供更多细节”。 北京认为台湾是中国领土，并誓言要让这个自治岛屿与大陆“统一”，必要时会使用武力。特别是自美国前众议院议长南希·佩洛西 2022 年访问台北以来，解放军在台湾频繁进行军事演习，加大了对台湾的压力。 在台北和华盛顿的反应中，印度尼西亚海军表示，其与中国海军的活动“本质上不是战斗活动”，并且“无意进行战斗训练”。 台湾淡江大学国际事务与战略研究所副教授林英宇告诉德国之声，中国与印尼的演习没有什么战术意义。 他说：“这不像联合海上演习那么实际，但中国希望宣示其在该海域的能力。” 不过，日本国际问题研究所研究台印尼关系的客座研究员拉蒂·卡比纳瓦(Ratih Kabinawa)告诉德国之声，无论演习的意义如何，印尼都应该预料到台湾会做出一些反应。 “无论你喜欢与否，印度尼西亚现在都被拖入了这种地缘政治游戏，”她说。 卡比纳瓦补充说，此次演习是中国迄今为止用来证明其恐吓台湾合理性的最低级别的海军活动之一。 她说：“印度尼西亚在这方面也必须保持谨慎。”她补充说，雅加达应该“不要太天真”，认为参加与中国的“定期演习”不会引起人们的担忧……

body.en:
The family of slain Australian aid worker Zomi Frankcom say they will continue their fight for justice, with missing drone audio remaining one of the central unanswered questions about her death.

Israel this week announced it would not prosecute those responsible for the killing of Frankcom and six of her World Central Kitchen colleagues in Gaza in April 2024, despite conceding "serious failures" that led to the mistaken-identity drone strikes by the Israel Defense Force (IDF) .

On Thursday, Foreign Minister Penny Wong said the decision was an "outrage" , and she had no confidence in the IDF's Military Advocate General's two-year investigation "given the many unanswered questions".

Among the unresolved issues is a missing piece of drone footage audio, which Israel refused to hand over to Australia's independent inquiry, headed by retired Air Chief Marshal Mark Binskin, despite requests by the federal government.

According to his report — which found the killing was due to mistaken identity and procedural failings but not a deliberate targeting of aid workers — Binskin was given access to 90 minutes of unedited drone footage, but it did not include an audio track.

Prime Minister Anthony Albanese renewed calls for the audio to be released in parliamentary Question Time on Thursday, saying it's part of the transparency Australia has called for "from day one".

Israeli ambassador to Australia Hillel Newman on Friday told ABC radio the audio may contain "intelligence information" and there was nothing in it to cast doubt on the findings which cleared the IDF of criminal misconduct.

In a statement on Thursday, Frankcom's family called on the government to continue pressing Israel to release the audio and to "pursue all available legal avenues for an independent and credible investigation to be conducted".

However Dr Emily Crawford, an international law professor at the University of Sydney, said Australia's options were limited.

"In all states, the scope to argue that national security grounds required for information not to be released, they're fairly paramount," she told SBS News.

"We've seen that the Netanyahu government is reluctant to assist in these kinds of things, so I can't imagine there's really going to be any movement on that."

The missing audio is just one of the unanswered questions surrounding the strike, with Wong saying the IDF had failed to explain how two strikes occurred after the initial strike, in breach of the IDF's rules of engagement.

summary.en: Discoveries from Europe's shrinking rivers highlight environmental challenges that extend globally, prompting other regions like Australia to observe and learn.

body.en:
In northern Bulgaria, water in the Danube River has fallen so low that scientists say an ancient mammal has once again been exposed to the world.

The remains of what is believed to be a woolly mammoth were uncovered in late July and hailed by historians as a "very important" discovery.

Near the Serbian village of Prahovo, the rusted vessels and broken masts of German warships also resurfaced from the riverbank this month.

"This has literally never happened before; these wrecks ... have never been visible like this. They've always been completely submerged; what we're seeing now is utterly unprecedented," he said.

The discoveries along Europe's second-longest river come as parts of central and eastern Europe experience prolonged summer heatwaves and drought conditions.

Armin Fojskic, a member of the Zenica Fishermen Association, said if conditions don't ease, he expects a large number of fish to die in European rivers.

"Low levels of water are critical for the fish, especially if it is extremely low, and these past days it has really been extremely low," Fojskic said.

"The main danger for fish is oxygenation of the river; when water flow drops, the river loses oxygen and fish start to suffocate."

According to the European Drought Observatory, about half of Europe and the United Kingdom experienced drought at various levels of intensity in July. Major wildfires have also burned across the continent .

But Peter Gleick, a hydro-climatologist and co-founder of the Pacific Institute in California, believes what Europe has experienced is not in line with normal weather fluctuations.

"Weather is always variable. We always have droughts. We always have floods somewhere at some time ... but what we're seeing now is extreme events worsened by human-caused climate change," Gleick told SBS News.

"We're dumping greenhouse gases into the atmosphere. We know that's warming the planet. We know that it's altering these extreme events by making them more extreme, more frequent, and more intense."

Gleick said the extreme patterns affecting rivers in Europe are similarly impacting water systems across the globe.

"In the western United States, the Colorado River, which is ... shared by seven [US] states and Mexico, is at record low levels," he said.

"Some of the largest reservoirs in the world are built on the Colorado River, and they're now at record lows."

body.en:
Two women at the centre of an investigation involving five players from the Sydney Swans AFL club were subjected to "abhorrent" actions, the women's lawyer alleges, further stating that they fear for their lives.

John Karantzis, acting for two of the three women involved, says more than five men were in the hotel room and accuses Swans hierarchy of not yet being fully transparent.

Sydney banned five players — Isaac Heeney, Chad Warner, Nick Blakey, Riley Bice and James Jordon — for the rest of the AFL season for breaching club standards at East Melbourne's Pullman Hotel on Monday morning.

Victoria Police Sex Crimes Squad detectives are investigating. No charges have been laid.

Karantzis said more than five men were in the room but refused to comment when asked if other Swans staff members were present.

"We have every reason to consider that reports to the contrary are simply false," the statement said.

"I've been at the football club for nine years. Every person within those four walls we value extremely highly and they have a massive say on our culture as a group," he said.

"We understand as leaders we need to lead that culture, but what we are going to do is back ourselves, and we're going to move forward and we're going to strive as strongly as we possibly can to repay the faith."

Karantzis said the two women he represented were in hiding and fearing violence.

"With what has been alleged, these women were subjected to the most disgusting actions and behaviour I have ever heard about in my 28 years as a lawyer," he said.

"And what they were subjected to, it is alleged, was demeaning, abhorrent and simply not moral or acceptable."

Karantzis, asked if the club hadn't yet been fully transparent, replied: "That is my understanding."

He couldn't detail specifics, citing the ongoing investigation which he said would take some time to complete.

title.zh: “他们会付出代价”：澳大利亚旅游热点的新旅游税

summary.en: Even travellers who have already paid in full could be caught out, according to an industry group.

body.en:
The Fijian government will introduce a new tourism services tax for large-scale tourism operators next month, with travel industry experts warning that the costs could be passed on to customers.

The 5 per cent tax will apply from 1 September. The change has been criticised by travel associations in Fiji, Australia and New Zealand, who claim they were not properly consulted.

The Australian Travel Industry Association (ATIA) said the measure could catch out travellers who have already booked trips to Fiji from September onward, as travel agents and operators face confusion over how to administer the tax.

"The design and roll out reflect a complete lack of understanding of how the travel booking ecosystem works, and it is travellers and travel businesses who will pay the price for that failure," ATIA CEO Dean Long said.

"Travellers are the ones left exposed. Families with September school holiday bookings already paid in full, and travellers on large group, corporate and film production bookings, are being asked to find extra money for a holiday they thought was settled months ago. That is not how you treat people who chose Fiji in good faith."

The change forms part of wider taxation amendments enacted as part of Fiji's 2026-2027 national budget, passed last month.

It will affect tourism operators — including hotel, tourism and cruise businesses — with an annual turnover above FJ$2 million (approximately $1.3 million).

According to Fijian finance minister Esrom Immanuel, revenue from the tax will be used to support Fiji Airways.

"The revenue generated will be ring-fenced and fully directed to Fiji Airways, which continues to face financial pressure from rising aviation fuel costs and its ongoing recovery from losses incurred during the COVID-19 pandemic," Immanuel told local media in June.

It's reported that the tourism tax will generate around FJ$70 million ($44.7 million) for the airline. The Fijian government is the largest shareholder of Fiji Airways.

ATIA confirmed it will meet with the Fijian government to discuss the tourism services tax, which it said arrived with "zero consultation".

Long said there is ongoing confusion over how the tax is collected, saying that members of the travel industry in Australia and New Zealand — which represent Fiji's largest tourism markets — were not consulted on the change.

"None of this needed to happen. The tax arrived with zero consultation with the travel industry in Australia or New Zealand despite the significant importance of these markets to Fiji," he said.

title.en: 'House of cards': The uncertain future of addiction help in Australia
title.zh: 《纸牌屋》：澳大利亚戒瘾帮助的不确定未来

summary.en: Half a million Australians are said to be exposed amid "significant uncertainty" about funding for the sector.
summary.zh: 这是一则来自澳洲栏目的新闻，重点涉及盼望、忍耐与重建。如需完整细节，请阅读英文原始报道。

body.en:
Half a million Australians have no access to desperately needed drug and alcohol addiction help, and funding uncertainty is intensifying the risk to existing services, a peak health provider warns.

The Australasian Therapeutic Communities Association (ATCA) fears that funding for many services is "a house of cards" that will collapse if federal funding is cut or not renewed.

ATCA chair Gerard Byrne said its members, who provide residential therapy, outreach and day programs, were reporting increases in waiting lists and waiting times.

"They turn up in hospitals, in police stations, in courts, in prison, in homeless services, in domestic and family violence services," he said.

Your trusted source for staying up-to-date with the world around you. Get free daily news updates and analysis, straight to your inbox.

"But they're not going there for the drug and alcohol problem. They're going there because all of those other things were happening for them because they couldn't get the drug and alcohol service."

ATCA executive officer Michelle Ridley said half a million Australians needing drug and alcohol treatment were missing out, and the issue was most acute in regional and remote areas.

"There is significant uncertainty about future funding for the sector and without confirmation of ongoing funding, some services undoubtedly face very hard decisions about their future admissions," she said.

"Our members are operating in an environment of significant pressure due to increasing demand for alcohol and other drug treatment services, workforce challenges, and uncertainty about future funding arrangements.."

Following a review of the federal Drug and Alcohol Program, the federal government extended existing grants until the end of June 2027.

Byrne said the sector needed the grant opportunities for the next round of three-year grant agreements to be released soon.

"The uncertainty is in what the future will be after the application process, because we're funded up until June 2027, but our members don't know what's happening after that," he said.

"DAP funding usually part funds programs along with the state and territory governments, so you get this house of cards situation where if you take one funding stream away or reduce it, the other funding streams are at risk because the financial sustainability is not there."

Readers struggling with their use of alcohol and other substances can contact the National Alcohol and Other Drug Hotline on 1800 250 015 for free and confidential support 24 hours a day, 7 days a week. More information is available via Lifeline .

title.en: 'Impact across the board': Australia's housing downturn enters a new phase
title.zh: “全面影响”：澳大利亚房地产低迷进入新阶段

summary.en: Housing prices in capital cities have been in decline. Now, the downturn has spread further.
summary.zh: 这是一则来自澳洲栏目的新闻，重点涉及管家责任、供应与公共福祉。如需完整细节，请阅读英文原始报道。

body.en:
The Southern Highlands property market has long attracted Australians seeking a tree-change — but Duncan Hill believes the NSW region has now become a prime buyer's market.

"We're definitely seeing a buying opportunity ... it's probably the best time that I've seen in the last five years," Hill told SBS News.

He founded Duncan Hill Property, based in the Southern Highlands town of Bowral, in 2013. Since then, Hill has witnessed changes to the regional housing market .

"We did see [housing price] growth of about 30 per cent over the last five years, but then it's declined now by about two to three per cent over the last 12 months."

That shift is consistent with Cotality's latest quarterly regional market update, which found Australia's housing market downturn is no longer confined to capital cities.

The property analytics firm examined Australia's 50 largest non-capital regional markets in the three months to July 2026. It found that regional dwelling values declined modestly by 0.1 per cent, compared with a 2.5 per cent fall across the combined capital cities over the same period.

Of the 50 markets analysed, Cotality found that 47 significant urban areas had slower growth, while 22 recorded a decline in home values.

The update did note that regional markets remained more resilient to change and typically outperformed capital cities.

Gerard Burg, head of research at Cotality Australia, said the results speak to recent pressures that have built up in the national housing market.

"A lot of buyers have been pushed out by the affordability pressures and by the increases in interest rates that we've seen so far," Burg told SBS News.

The Reserve Bank of Australia (RBA) has raised interest rates three times this year as it attempts to bring inflation back towards the midpoint of its 2-3 per cent target range. At its most recent meeting, the RBA board unanimously decided to keep interest rates on hold at 4.35 per cent.

But Burg believes recent rate hikes, compounded by a cost of living crisis , mean "fewer buyers nationally [are] ready to make a purchase".

"We're seeing this reduced level of competition. We've seen houses on the market for longer, and buyers who remain in the market now have more ability to negotiate, and that's leading to this situation where values are starting to push lower."

Anne Flaherty, senior economist at REA Group, also cited changes in the housing market to federal housing tax reforms announced in the May budget — including an overhaul to negative gearing and capital gains tax (CGT) rules — set to come into effect next year.

title.en: Albanese wanted 'full accountability' from Israel. Instead, Australia is 'outraged'
title.zh: 阿尔巴尼斯希望以色列承担“全部责任”。相反，澳大利亚感到“愤怒”

summary.en: Outrage over Israel's response to aid worker Zomi Frankcom's killing is the latest flashpoint in a relationship that's no longer warm.
summary.zh: 这是一则来自澳洲栏目的新闻，重点涉及和平与克制。如需完整细节，请阅读英文原始报道。

body.en:
Israel's decision not to pursue criminal proceedings over the killing of Australian aid worker Zomi Frankcom has sparked "outrage" from the federal government, signalling a new low for relations between the two countries.

The decision comes after almost three years of increasingly strained ties, with Australia moving from backing Israel after the October 7 attacks to i mposing sanctions on Israeli government ministers and recognising a Palestinian state.

Despite previously conceding there had been "serious failures", the Israeli Defense Forces (IDF) on Wednesday announced it would not prosecute those responsible for the death of Frankcom and six of her World Central Kitchen colleagues in an IDF strike in Gaza in April 2024.

Foreign Minister Penny Wong said the decision "falls far short of the accountability we expect" in some of her most critical comments against Israel since the Gaza war began.

Asked about Australia's relationship with Israel, Wong said it was facing a "difficult time".

She said the federal government only became aware of the decision moments before it was publicly announced, and it was "especially insulting" to Frankcom's family that it came on World Humanitarian Day, a point echoed by Zomi's brother Mal in a statement.

The Greens called for the Israeli ambassador, Hillel Newman, who was summoned by the government for an explanation on Thursday, to be expelled.

Opposition defence spokesperson James Paterson said the news was "incredibly concerning", but he needed to receive a full briefing before making further comment.

Frankcom and her colleagues were travelling in a marked aid convoy in Khan Younis, southern Gaza, when they were hit by three Israeli drone strikes on 1 April 2024.

The Israeli military initially said the convoy had been mistaken for a group of Hamas fighters before later acknowledging the vehicles had been misidentified and there had been serious failures in the decision-making leading to the attack.

Australia and Israel have historically enjoyed warm relations, with Australia supporting Israel at international forums such as the United Nations.

title.en: Australia's new media bargaining laws put pressure on tech platforms to pay for news
title.zh: 澳大利亚新媒体讨价还价法给科技平台带来支付新闻费用的压力

summary.en: The passage of the News Bargaining laws comes just 24 hours after laws restricting gambling advertisements.
summary.zh: 这是一则来自澳洲栏目的新闻，重点涉及公义、尊严与问责。如需完整细节，请阅读英文原始报道。

body.en:
The Australian government passed legislation on Thursday that will force tech giants to pay millions of dollars in levies if they fail to strike commercial deals with local media outlets for news on their platforms.

The News Bargaining Incentive taxes the companies 2.5 per cent on their advertising revenues unless they strike agreements.

Proceeds from the scheme would be directed to local Australian news outlets, whose content helps drive user engagement and advertising revenue on the tech firms' platforms.

The levy applies to Meta, Alphabet's Google, TikTok and Microsoft's LinkedIn, covering companies with a "significant" social media or search service in Australia, and local advertising revenue exceeding $250 million.

Platforms can avoid the charge by reaching agreements with at least eight different publishers by the end of their reporting period. The value of those deals would be offset against their levy liability.

The deals must support the production of news content or relate to news content produced by the publishers being made available online by the platform, the legislation said.

Spending with large publishers carries a 150 per cent offset, while spending with small and medium-sized outlets carries a 200 per cent offset.

"The legislation is here, and the message to platforms to pursue commercial deals is clear. Deals will need to be finalised before the end of a digital platform's financial reporting period to be used to offset their liability in that period," the government said in a statement.

"This is an important day for Australian news businesses and Australian journalism."

The passage of the News Bargaining Incentive comes one day after parliament passed laws restricting gambling advertisements.
